title: Feature Catalyst Notebook — Micro-Response Tiers & Dev Ergonomics
content:
Goal: sketch a lightweight set of developer-facing controls and server-side primitives that let apps trade response fidelity for cost/latency in a predictable, composable way. Keep initial surface tiny so we can ship experiments in 6 weeks.

Why: customers keep asking for cheaper, faster fallback behavior beyond swapping model sizes: a smaller API surface for teams to express degraded-but-useful responses, plus defaults that play well with streaming and stateful sessions.

High-level idea (one-liner): 'Micro-response tiers' — request-level hints + small server-side modules (presets) that transform prompts or post-process outputs to meet a budget target while preserving core utility. Think "sketch", "concise", "safe-burst" presets.

Principles:
- Explicit, composable: presets are named and combinable (e.g., concise + safe-burst).
- Predictable economics: devs understand per-response token/cost delta roughly before calling.
- Low cognitive load: default out-of-the-box presets should cover 80% of use cases.
- Minimal infra changes for rollout: route to existing model variants where possible.

Rough PRD outline:
- Problem statement: high-perf apps need deterministic levers to control cost/latency at request time without rewriting prompts or managing model variants manually.
- Objectives (OKRs):
  * O1: Reduce median token cost for sampled customer workloads by 30% for non-critical responses within 8 weeks.
  * O2: 75% of internal devs can integrate micro-tiers with <= 15 lines of code.
- Success metrics:
  * adoption: number of routes using presets
  * economics: delta in tokens/response and latency p50/p95 when using presets
  * quality: human eval drift on key prompts (no more than 10% drop vs baseline for accepted use cases)
- Scope (MVP):
  * API: extra query param or top-level field: "micro_tier": "concise" | "sketch" | "default" | "budget:<tokens>"
  * Server behavior: map to one of: (a) model variant + prompt wrapper; (b) post-process compression; (c) combine with cached summary prefix.
  * Console: per-route toggle and per-tier readout of estimated cost multiplier.
  * Observability: token/cost breakdown by tier, error/quality sampling.
- Out of scope for MVP: multi-tenant custom presets, RL-based rewrite, UI for editing presets (post-MVP).

Developer-facing API sketches:
- REST/SDK example: {"model":"rw-1-large","input":"...","micro_tier":"concise"} -> server applies concise wrapper and uses rw-1-small as fallback in overloaded buckets.
- More explicit budget mode: {"micro_tier":"budget:150"} -> server ensures approximate token budget for generated content (best-effort).

User stories:
- As a product engineer, I want a preset that shortens assistant replies for mobile so that my app reduces cost and preserves latency during high traffic. Acceptance: response length reduced by ~40% with semantic preservation for 80% of test prompts.
- As an SRE, I want predictable fallbacks so that under load we degrade gracefully instead of timing out. Acceptance: under simulated 2x load, 90% requests hit lower-cost path with no client error.
- As a platform engineer, I want per-tier telemetry so we can show customers cost impact and let them tune. Acceptance: console shows tiered token metrics and ability to filter traces by micro_tier.

Quality & evaluation plan:
- Create small eval suite (40 prompts across 3 verticals: search, assistant, summarization).
- For each prompt, track: baseline tokens, concise tokens, sketch tokens, human-rated usefulness (1–5).
- Gate: if mean usefulness drop > 0.5 for any vertical, block rollout for that vertical.

Experiment matrix (fast iterations):
- Axis A: Implementation strategy: model-switch vs. prompt-wrap vs. post-process compressor.
- Axis B: Tier semantics: concise (aggressive truncation), sketch (bullet summary), default (no change).
- Axis C: Traffic routing: opt-in client param vs. route default vs. server autodetect.
- Quick experiments: run A/B on 1% traffic for each combinator with synthetic load and track latency/cost/quality.

Open questions / risks:
- How to surface "estimated cost multiplier" when server-side heuristics vary at runtime? (approximate bands vs exact)
- Budget-mode semantics: how precise should budget:NN be? Best-effort or hard cap?
- Interaction with streaming: how do we handle prefix caching + short form generation while streaming tokens?
- Abuse vectors: low-fidelity presets could encourage unsafe truncation; need safety checks.

Implementation sketch & rollout plan (6-week sprint roadmap):
- Week 1: spec finalization, pick two presets (concise, sketch), add micro_tier param to API surface (SDK stubs).
- Week 2: server prototype: prompt-wrap + model-affinity mapping, add basic cost estimator.
- Week 3: run internal eval suite, tune wrappers (temperature, max_tokens).
- Week 4: add console readouts and per-route toggle behind feature flag.
- Week 5: 1% public A/B with customers who opt-in via support. Collect metrics and human labels.
- Week 6: expand to 10% and decide GA vs iterate.

Monitoring & rollback criteria:
- Rollback if p95 latency increases > 20% for affected routes, or error rate increases by +0.5%.
- Rollback if human eval shows > 10% critical failure (incoherent or unsafe) in production sampling.

Engineering notes / low-level ideas:
- Use lightweight server-side rewrite templates rather than heavy model-based compression initially (faster iteration).
- Leverage existing KV cache for prefix compression: store compacted summaries and stitch at request time.
- Add a cheap token-estimator function in runtime to provide per-request cost bands for telemetry.

Next steps (short actionable list):
- [ ] Sync with SRE (Arjun) about routing and feature-flag strategy.
- [ ] Build eval suite and pick 40 prompts (Maya to own curation).
- [ ] Prototype SDK flag for micro_tier (Lena to add JS/Go stubs).
- [ ] Draft user-facing docs + examples for console.

Notes to self (brain-dump):
- Keep naming simple: "concise"/"sketch"/"budget" are intuitive. Avoid "low-fidelity" wording in docs.
- Consider "composable modifiers" later: e.g., concise + preserve-named-entities.
- Think about a "guided migration" for customers with heavy token use (automated recommendations via Optimize).

Short-term thought: this might be a lightweight wedge into Optimize and Console: if we can show clear cost reduction with small quality tradeoffs and great telemetry, sales/CS will have an easy story to move customers to Dedicated/Reserved tiers with predictable economics.

End of notes.
